metadata.note: The Delaware and Northern (1911-1942) and its predecessor the Delaware and Eastern (1906-1911) ran East Branch (junction with the New York, Ontario and Western) - Downsville - Margaretville - Arkville (junction with the Ulster and Delaware), 37.52 mi down the East Branch of the Delaware in Delaware County, NY, with an 8.38 mi branch from Andes Junction to Andes. Only this first link of a planned Wilkes-Barre - Hancock - Schenectady coal road was built; the Hancock & East Branch and Schenectady & Margaretville never carried trains and the Andes - Bovina extension was dropped. Last passenger run 17 Oct 1942; much of the valley now lies under the Pepacton Reservoir. Research report: research/branches/delaware_and_northern_railroad.txt.
sources: https://trainweb.us/delawarenorthern/history_best.htm -- BEST (Gerald M. Best, The Ulster & Delaware ... Railroad Through the Catskills, 1972, D&N chapter)
https://trainweb.us/delawarenorthern/history_horton.htm -- HORTON (Gertrude Fitch Horton, The Delaware & Northern and the Towns It Served, 1989)
https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/newyorkstaterrs2.pdf -- FOW (Fowler, sections 99 and 99A; station lists and mileages only)
metadata.operator_split: 14 Oct 1911: Delaware and Eastern -> Delaware and Northern (foreclosure sale 16 Aug 1911 and a new company). The main line is drawn as two features with identical geometry, Delaware and Eastern 1906-1911 and Delaware and Northern 1911-1942, each in its own colour (Rule 4). Not splits: the 1907 D&E Railroad -> Railway merger with its own subsidiaries, the 1910 and 1921 receiverships, and Rosoff's 1929 rename to Delaware and Northern Railway.
metadata.colors: Neither company had a colour anywhere in data/ (checked programmatically across every layer's company strings). Delaware and Eastern #8A5A2B and Delaware and Northern #4F6D2F are new and used by no other feature in data/.
omitted: Delaware and Northern: Andes Branch (report block [4], drawable NONE): no source found dates a passenger train on the branch in any year 1911-1925; the branch closed outright in late March/April 1925 (HORTON; BEST 'April 1925'; ICC Finance Docket 4675 decided 28 Apr 1925), which is only a ceiling. Not drawn.
Hancock & East Branch, Schenectady & Margaretville, Andes - Bovina extension: never built / never carried trains.
Informal late-1905 rides on planked flat cars between completed sections (HORTON): untimetabled, not drawn.
not_yet_sourced: OPEN: Delaware and Eastern Andes Branch drawn 1907-1908 only. 1908 is the last confirmed passenger year (BEST), not a known end; passenger service very likely continued 1909-1911 and into the D&N era but is not sourced. ICC Finance Docket 4675 (1925), any 1909-1924 Official Guide D&N table, or the Catskill Mountain News (nyshistoricnewspapers.org) should settle it.

Delaware and Northern Andes Branch (1911 to at most 1925) NOT DRAWN: no D&N-era passenger evidence found; when passenger trains (or a mixed) stopped on the branch is unknown. Wikipedia's Andes station page carries an unexplained 'closed in 1921' category.
Main-line headways and both speeds are estimates; motor-car frequency conflicts (HORTON one daily round trip vs Wikipedia two).
No mid-life timetable (1912-1925) has been seen for the main line; continuity rests on HORTON and BEST.
Receivership date conflict: 25 Feb 1910 (BEST) vs 10 Mar 1910 (HORTON). Sale of the reservoir lands to New York City: 1939 (BEST) vs 1942 (Wikipedia lead).
Positions of the drowned stations (Pepacton, Shavertown, Union Grove, Arena) are milepost-interpolated along an OSM reconstruction, not located.

properties.line: Delaware and Eastern: East Branch – Arkville
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE, unsourced: no in-era running time found. Mountain-valley steam mixed train (4-4-0 with one coach, one baggage car and freight cars, HORTON); 30 km/h assumed.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-10-18), routed with opstrace.py over the road's own OSM ways. OSM tags almost none of the D&N with old_railway_operator (probed 'D&N', 'Delaware.*Northern', 'D&E', 'Delaware.*Eastern': only 4 ways, as 'Delaware and Northern Railroad'); most are named name='Delaware and Northern Railroad' with abandoned:railway=rail or razed:railway=rail, so the tracer's Operator was extended to own ways by that name. OpenHistoricalMap was queried over the whole valley (41.97,-75.16,42.21,-74.60) and holds no railway ways there.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 37.2 mi against 37.52 mi documented (TrainWeb route page; Fowler 37.5) = -0.8%. No straight-line leg; 100% on OSM ways named or tagged for the Delaware and Northern. East Branch - Downsville dam (c.15.1 mi) follows the surviving grade: OSM ways 47175369, 225144162 (Bump Road), 225144157 (Tomannex Public Forest Access Road), 842895760 (path) and 1095782605 (abandoned:railway). Downsville dam - Arkville (22.2 mi) is ONE OSM way, 843180148, tagged razed:railway=rail: a mapper's reconstruction, not a surviving grade. About 16.1 mi of it lies inside the Pepacton Reservoir polygon (OSM relation 4057387) - from just above the Downsville dam to the reservoir's upper end below Dunraven - so that drowned leg (Pepacton, Shavertown, Andes Junction, Union Grove, Arena) cannot be checked on the ground or against OHM; treat it as approximate to a few hundred metres. The remaining c.4.7 mi Dunraven - Margaretville - Arkville on that way is also a reconstruction, above water. Check points: the Andes-branch junction node (601334700, where the OSM Andes branch leaves the razed main line) falls at 25.6 traced mi from East Branch vs 25.45 documented; Harvard 0.6 km, Shinhopple 0.4 km, Downsville 1.1 km, Dunraven 1.2 km and Margaretville 0.1 km from the line (village place nodes, not depot sites). Drowned stations (Pepacton, Shavertown, Union Grove, Arena) have no surviving place node; their positions in metadata.station_pins are interpolated along the trace from the TrainWeb mileposts, not located. The line starts at the D&N's own end of track beside the NYO&W at East Branch and ends at the razed way's end at Arkville beside the U&D yard; it does not run onto either connecting railroad. No later realignment of the D&N is known, so the drawn alignment is the line's own (1906-1942) alignment as reconstructed in OSM.

segments.note: Report block [1]. Delaware and Eastern Railroad (from 17 May 1907 Delaware and Eastern Railway, a merger with its own paper subsidiaries - same operator). First timetable 5 June 1906, Shavertown - Arkville (14 mi, HORTON); last spike at Downsville and through service East Branch - Arkville from 17 Nov 1906 (BEST, HORTON; The Sun 18 Nov 1906: 'a through train ran over the Delaware and Eastern Railroad ... from East Branch on the Ontario and Western to Arkville on the Ulster and Delaware'). Both openings fall in 1906, so one span is drawn over the whole line from 1906 - the East Branch - Shavertown part actually began only in Nov 1906. Informal 1905 rides on planked flat cars (HORTON) were not timetabled service and are not drawn. Mail contract 13 May 1907. Receivership Feb/Mar 1910 (BEST 25 Feb vs HORTON 10 Mar - conflict, immaterial to the years); foreclosure sale 16 Aug 1911. Ends 1911 because the OPERATOR changed (Delaware and Northern incorporated 14 Oct 1911, The Sun 15 Oct 1911), not because service stopped - it continues in the Delaware and Northern feature. Headway is an ESTIMATE: Best and Horton describe a single daily passenger train each way; no timetable seen.
sources: Segment-level: HORTON (5 Jun 1906 first timetable; 17 Nov 1906 last spike; 14 Oct 1911 D&N incorporation), BEST (17 Nov 1906 completion and passenger service), The Sun 18 Nov 1906 p.6 (through train), The Sun 15 Oct 1911 p.14 (reorganization). Headway not sourced (estimate).

segments.note: Report block [2]. Delaware and Northern Railroad, incorporated at Albany 14 Oct 1911 as 'the reorganized Delaware and Eastern' (The Sun 15 Oct 1911; HORTON); receivers again from 16 Mar 1921; bought by Samuel R. Rosoff 20 Dec 1928 (BEST) and renamed Delaware and Northern Railway from 1 Jan 1929 (HORTON) - same display name and trains, so not a split. Steam passenger trains (mixed consists) from the 1911 reorganization until the Brill motor car took over on 25 Feb 1926 (HORTON). Passenger traffic was lost to the automobile after the 1922 concrete highway (HORTON). Headway is an ESTIMATE: one passenger train each way daily per HORTON's and BEST's descriptions; no D&N timetable seen.
sources: Segment-level: SUN-1911 (The Sun 15 Oct 1911 p.14, incorporation 14 Oct 1911), HORTON (incorporation; Brill car in service from 25 Feb 1926). No source dates any specific 1912-1925 timetable; continuity of service across these years rests on HORTON and BEST's narrative. Headway not sourced (estimate).

segments.note: Report block [2]. Delaware and Northern Railroad, incorporated at Albany 14 Oct 1911 as 'the reorganized Delaware and Eastern' (The Sun 15 Oct 1911; HORTON); receivers again from 16 Mar 1921; bought by Samuel R. Rosoff 20 Dec 1928 (BEST) and renamed Delaware and Northern Railway from 1 Jan 1929 (HORTON) - same display name and trains, so not a split. Brill gasoline motor car (65 ft, 250 hp Winton engine, bought Feb 1926, No. 10, nicknamed the 'Red Heifer') in service 25 Feb 1926 - 19 Oct 1942 on the old steam schedule, carrying an RPO and school pupils (HORTON); a locomotive and 'the old combination car' substituted for three days after the 5 Sep 1934 accident near Arena. BEST notes a daily school train after 1928. Last passenger run 17 Oct 1942 (HORTON); abandonment notice posted at the stations 16 Oct 1942 (BEST); the last movement of any kind, an empty boxcar for the U&D on 19 Oct 1942, is two days of freight-only working below year resolution - no freight tail is drawn. Rails lifted 1942-43; the valley was flooded by the Pepacton Reservoir (dam finished c.1955). Headway is an ESTIMATE and a source CONFLICT: HORTON describes one daily round trip (car based at Downsville: Downsville - Arkville - East Branch - Arkville - Downsville); Wikipedia says two round trips a day. Neither is a timetable; 1440 follows HORTON.
sources: Segment-level: HORTON (Brill car 25 Feb 1926 - 19 Oct 1942; last passenger run 17 Oct 1942; daily pattern), BEST (abandonment notice 16 Oct 1942; Red Heifer replaced steam passenger trains). Headway not sourced (estimate; HORTON vs Wikipedia conflict).

properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE, unsourced: steep branch (Andes c.400 ft above Andes Junction in nine miles, HORTON) worked by a mixed train; 25 km/h assumed.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-10-18), routed with opstrace.py over the road's own OSM ways. OSM tags almost none of the D&N with old_railway_operator (probed 'D&N', 'Delaware.*Northern', 'D&E', 'Delaware.*Eastern': only 4 ways, as 'Delaware and Northern Railroad'); most are named name='Delaware and Northern Railroad' with abandoned:railway=rail or razed:railway=rail, so the tracer's Operator was extended to own ways by that name. OpenHistoricalMap was queried over the whole valley (41.97,-75.16,42.21,-74.60) and holds no railway ways there.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 8.3 mi against 8.38 mi documented from Andes Junction (TrainWeb route page; Fowler 9.1 from Union Grove) = -1%. No straight-line leg; 100% on OSM ways for the D&N Andes branch: 47175379, 1095782604, 243737956 (abandoned bridge), 243737957 (all name='Delaware and Northern Railroad', abandoned:railway=rail) and 875807365, 222218274 (Andes Rail Trail, old_railway_operator='Delaware and Northern Railroad'). Starts at OSM node 601334700, where way 47175379 leaves the razed main-line way 843180148; that junction is itself under the Pepacton Reservoir (the first c.0.6 mi of the branch to the reservoir's Tremper Kill arm is drowned and rests on the same OSM reconstruction). Ends at the end of the Andes Rail Trail beside the 1907 Andes depot. The line's own 1907 alignment.

segments.note: Report block [3], drawable 1907-1908 [OPEN]. Andes Junction - Pleasant Valley - Wolf Hollow - Kaufman's - Andes, up the Tremper Kill; trains worked out of Union Grove (Fowler measures the branch from Union Grove). 'Regular train service to Andes began on March 23, 1907' (HORTON; same date BEST); excursion 25 Mar 1907; mail from 13 May 1907. A 4-4-0 could take one coach, one baggage car and two freight cars (HORTON) - a mixed train. BEST: 'in 1908 a passenger train made a daily run up the Andes branch.' OPEN END: 1908 is the last CONFIRMED passenger year, NOT a known end. Service very likely continued to the 1911 reorganization and into the Delaware and Northern era (the branch closed outright in late March/April 1925), but no source found dates a passenger train on the branch after 1908. Do not extend without evidence. Headway is an ESTIMATE from BEST's 'daily run'.
sources: Segment-level: HORTON (regular service from 23 Mar 1907), BEST (23 Mar 1907 opening; 'in 1908 a passenger train made a daily run up the Andes branch'). End year is the last confirmed year, not a sourced end. Headway not sourced beyond 'daily' (estimate).
